hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Bulky and heavy freight
hits.snippet:
Bulky and heavy freight
Rerouting bulky freight (over 30 kg billable, any side over 100 cm, or a combined size over 200 cm) is uneconomical and risky. Keep the shipment on its original route, tell the customer about the delay and compensate

hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Standard delays
hits.snippet:
Standard delays
For all other late orders, keep the shipment on its route, send a clear and empathetic update with the new delivery window, and apply the compensation tier that matches the number of days late.

hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Long delays
hits.snippet:
Long delays
Any order more than fourteen days late gets a no-fee cancellation offer in addition to compensation, whatever its product type.

hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Reroute via alternate seller
hits.snippet:
Reroute via alternate seller
If the order has not yet been handed to the carrier and the same product is sold by another seller outside the disrupted area, fulfil it from that seller when all of the following hold:

hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Reroute via alternate route
hits.snippet:
Reroute via alternate route
Small parcels (up to 5 kg billable and 60 cm on the longest side) that are blocked at origin or on the linehaul can move to an alternate carrier or air corridor. This costs about 60% more freight and adds one day

summary.headline: Last-mile courier strike in Rio de Janeiro impacts 81 orders over 3.0 days.
summary.narrative: A recent disruption caused by a last-mile courier strike in Rio de Janeiro has placed 270 orders in scope, leading to 81 orders delayed and 81 customers delayed across 65 sellers and 81 SKUs delayed. The total GMV delayed is R$ 16,524.62, with an average hold days of 3.2. Among the delayed volume, 23 orders are breaching promise, representing 28 percent of delayed breaching, while 9 orders are newly breaching. Severity is distributed across 2 critical, 9 high, 18 medium, and 52 low incidents, with Health Beauty leading categories at 13 delayed orders, followed by Watches Gifts with 12 and Sports Leisure with 9. Origin states contributing to delayed items include SP with 42, RJ with 24, and MG with 4. To address this situation with an estimated mitigation cost of R$ 924.05, operations will apply specific decisions comprising 23 for delay with compensation, 199 for monitor only (no customer contact), and 48 for proactive heads-up (still on time) to secure the recovery days of 1.0.
recommendations: Assign customer care to call the 2 critical-severity customers before the emails go out.
Coordinate with last-mile partners in the affected destinations (RJ (81) delayed orders) to queue deliveries for the first days after the disruption, oldest promises first.
Review and approve the customer emails, starting with the 23 orders that will miss the promised date (sorted by severity on the Customer emails tab).
